extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, small startups, individual bloggers and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and modular 'building blocks' for creating a customized code of ethics for news organizations, startups, and individual journalists/bloggers so the code reflects their practices, tools and principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the fundamentals that should apply to all journalists; presented as a core principle to be included in any ethics code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly named among the fundamentals for all journalists; the code should prohibit plagiarism and set expectations for attribution and original reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptly correct errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a baseline obligation for journalists; codes should specify error-correction practices and timelines for correcting mistakes publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide customization and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Give journalists ownership and flexibility in creating an ethics code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project recognizes no single ethics code fits everyone; the best way to secure adoption is to let organizations and individuals customize their codes so they feel ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific building blocks to customize the remainder of the code
rubrics_metrics.description: After laying out fundamentals, offer a set of specific 'building blocks' that let you customize the remainder of the code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides modular options to tailor sections of a code to the organization's size, technology, mission and context rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce a comprehensive, personalized statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a comprehensive, personalized statement of how you see journalism ethics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once worked through, the site aims for users to have a complete personalized code that reflects their principles and can guide behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly post the code and live by it
rubrics_metrics.description: A code that can be publicly posted and lived by
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages transparency (posting the code publicly) and emphasizes that having a code is meaningful only if behavior aligns with it over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the code to spark discussion of ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you don’t create a full code, reviewing these materials should spark discussions of the most important ethical issues for your organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site is intended as a conversation starter; organizations should use it to initiate internal deliberations about practical ethics decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult wider sources and existing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Look beyond the project's building blocks to the sources consulted and to the much wider range of codes throughout the world of journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages users to review other national and organizational codes and the project's source materials when constructing or revising their own code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize codes are a guide; judge by behavior and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing and posting an ethics code doesn’t solve every issue; the ultimate test remains how you behave over time and the reliability of what you report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code should be treated as a guiding star; acknowledge that imperfect compliance may occur, but emphasize accountability, consistent behavior, and reliability of reporting as the true measures of ethical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address conflicts between organizational pressures and principles (clause of conscience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that political and financial pressures may force violations; a code can make clear when journalists are being asked to act contrary to their principles and some agreements recognize a 'clause of conscience'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include provisions or processes for resolving principled conflicts (e.g., mechanisms for recusal, protest, or negotiated exit); consider whether collective-bargaining or contractual protections like a clause of conscience are relevant.
